HEEWON STYLE — a premium KOREAN WEBTOON / MANHWA splash illustration of a group, lit with cinematic tenebrism. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). FULL-FIGURE GROUP SHOT, all five full-length, every face readable, low worm’s-eye angle. DRAW IT EXACTLY IN THE STYLE OF THE ATTACHED CHARACTER SHEET: the same clean confident black ink linework, the same manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair). It must read as an INKED DRAWING: visible line strokes everywhere — bold tapered contour lines around every figure, drawn fold lines in the silk and armour, hair drawn as inked strands, a little cross-hatching and line shading in the shadows — then flat cel-shading in two or three tones per colour, no airbrushed gradients. Each face must be recognisably the character drawn on the sheet, wearing the same clothes. NOT realistic, NOT an oil painting, NOT photoreal, NOT painterly, NOT a 3D render, no skin pores or photographic texture. ONLY THESE FIVE PEOPLE in the frame. THE BAEKJE RESTORATION ARMY'S FIVE CAPTAINS STRIKE A FLAMBOYANT, SYNCHRONISED TEAM POSE like a vintage anime special-forces squad roll call — each a different eccentric, theatrical, self-important pose, all showing off to the camera, staggered in a V. Boksin centre, one fist thrust at the lens, roaring; Dochim crouched on one knee, staff planted, one palm raised in a mudra, serene smile; Sangji half-turned, glaring over his shoulder, spear angled across; Sangya leaning back on one leg with both arms flung wide like wings; Prince Pung highest at the back, hand on hip, pointing at the sky, a little too eager, holding the pole of a torn plain yellow banner with NO writing. Comic pride. No swords drawn. Field behind: deep yellow-umber. CHARACTER SHEET (copy these faces, hair and clothes exactly): 1st face from the LEFT of the sheet = GWISHIL BOKSIN; 2nd face from the LEFT of the sheet = DOCHIM; 3rd face from the LEFT of the sheet = HUKCHI SANGJI; 4th face from the LEFT of the sheet = SATEK SANGYA; 5th face from the LEFT of the sheet = PRINCE PUNG. GWISHIL BOKSIN — Look: Shaven-headed Baekje general: bald crown with one long black topknot tail tied in red cord and streaming behind, heavy scowling brows, black moustache and pointed black beard. Dress: Black-lacquered lamellar with heavy rounded shoulder guards and bracers over a slate-blue wrapped robe, a grey-mauve sash knotted at the waist; a long red-lacquered shaft carried low in one fist. Colour #a8781f. | DOCHIM — Look: Shaven-headed monk-general in his forties: calm narrow eyes, faint smile, a small dark goatee. Dress: Ochre-gold monk robe under a red-orange kasaya fastened at the left shoulder with an iron ring; a long string of black 108 beads looped over one hand; a gilt monk staff with a ringed finial over the shoulder. Colour #a06a28. | HUKCHI SANGJI — Look: Hard-faced Baekje general: black moustache and short square beard, heavy brows, a glare under a black helm with a tall red plume. Dress: Black-lacquered lamellar armour with square shoulder guards over a maroon-red robe, a tan cross-strap and wide tan belt; a long spear with a gilt head over the shoulder; a ring-pommel sword at the hip. Colour #8a6b1f. | SATEK SANGYA — Look: Stocky harbour lord about forty: sea-tanned skin, shrewd narrow pricing eyes, flat unimpressed mouth, clipped black beard and moustache, thick neck. Dress: Deep red wide-sleeved Satek robe with a black crossed collar under a plain grey steel lamellar vest; a dark sash with a string of square-holed bronze coins and bamboo tally slips at the hip; a rolled harbour ledger in hand. Crown: the great-clan gilt crown (see NOBLE CROWN), no jougwan. Colour #b8933f. | PRINCE PUNG — Look: Prince years: smooth beardless face, soft eyes, black hair in a topknot bound with a red-and-gold cord and a gold pin. Dress: Red robe with black sleeves striped in gold, gold-brocade crossed collar, braided red-and-gold cord sash. Colour #e6c76a. LIGHT AND BACKGROUND (dark manhwa tenebrism, like a dramatic manhwa splash page): a MINIMAL MONOTONE background — one flat dark field in a single hue (the characters' colour deepened almost to black), at most a few soft wisps of smoke in that same hue; no set, no architecture, no landscape, no furniture, no props beyond what the characters hold or sit on; ONE hard directional light from the side or below carves the faces and silk in high contrast, the far side of each figure falling off into black shadow, a thin edge of the same light along the silhouettes; deep inky blacks, crisp highlights, strong cast shadows across the faces. Each person's colour is the colour of the light and the shadow-tint on them — never a glow aura or halo. BLOCKING, BODY LANGUAGE AND FACIAL EXPRESSIONS show the relationship at a glance. Faces and clothes from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. One of each person, never cloned. No text, no lettering, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark.
